latest_release.name: v0.43.0
latest_release.body:
### New Features

- Added **snapshot hints** for controls whose accessible name is empty or shared with another ref in the same snapshot. The hint follows the ref and lists the control's icon, image file, `data-testid`, `name` or `id`, and the text of the nearest row or list item (#2578)
- Added a **Modern Web Guidance skill** that retrieves Chrome's guidance for a task and checks the built page in agent-browser (#2577)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **commands on closed tabs** waiting for the timeout. A command whose tab closes before Chrome answers now fails with `Target closed: CDP session <id> detached` (#2576)
- Fixed **recordings with an emulated device scale**, which now capture at full density by switching to screenshots when a screencast frame is below the page's scale (#2572)

### Improvements

- Native binaries now ship as **per-platform packages**, so an install downloads only the binary for the host platform, and the global command links to it when install scripts are blocked (#2150)
- **Snapshots of large pages** parse the accessibility tree once, so they finish sooner (#2509)

### Documentation

- Added a **Modern Web Guidance** guide to the docs (#2546, #2573, #2575)

### Contributors

- @ctate
- @lahfir
- @shuding

detail.readme:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured. Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | |---|---|---| | Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) | | Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) | | Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) | | Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) | | Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) | | Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) | | Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) | | Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) | | Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `flow`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) | | Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) | | Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) | Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration). ## Platforms Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host. ## Development Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI pnpm link --global agent-browser install ``` Run the Rust checks from `cli/`: ```bash cargo fmt -- --check cargo clippy cargo test cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process. ## Documentation - [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference - [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration) - [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries - [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0
